solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Be critical of a Catholic institute in friendly Central American location

parts.note: to pan something is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: the Catholic and institute letters sit inside the word for friendly

parts.note: maty is British slang for friendly

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a Catholic institution in a welcoming spot in Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: This port city is the capital of Panama, a place in Central America.

clue.text: Too much French upset Stanley, for one

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: trop is French for too much

explanation.surface: Someone has had too much French and is upset with a man called Stanley.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley here is Port Stanley, capital of the Falkland Islands, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Stanley in the Falklands is an example of a harbour town, so Stanley is one such place.

clue.text: Recruits in order to have these?

definitions.text: Recruits in order to have these?

parts.words: Recruits in order to have these?
parts.note: recruits to a religious order are newcomers; read as two words the clue hints that members of a holy order have no sins

explanation.surface: A question about what recruits must have to be in order.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO VICES it says what those in a religious order should have; whole, it names the newcomers to that order.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcomers training to join a religious order are called by this name, and it splits into 'no' plus sins.

clue.text: Naughty Romeo stole bra — it should give support

indicators.note: naughty behaviour is disorderly, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A badly behaved Romeo makes off with a bra, which is meant to support.
explanation.walkthrough: The bra suggests physical support; the answer is emotional support.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that lifts spirits gives emotional encouragement, which is a kind of support.

clue.text: Code cracked by detective on the tail of classic English item of apparel

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of what follows
the code word is broken open and the detective is put into the gap

parts.note: taken as written
PI is a private investigator

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A detective cracks a code while following some classic English costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece was a pouch worn at the front of men's breeches, a historic piece of clothing.

clue.text: He is dumped by Theresa — not exactly a stunner

indicators.note: the remaining letters are not exactly in order, so they are rearranged
the word he is thrown out of the name Theresa

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is dumped by his girlfriend Theresa, who is not much of a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing HE from THERESA leaves TRESA, which 'not exactly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A taser is a stun gun, so it is literally a device that stuns.

clue.text: Black dog has lead for restraint

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A black dog is kept on a lead as a restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog's lead looks like a leash; it is the first letter of 'Black'.
explanation.definitionFit: A curb is a check or limit, the same as a restraint.

clue.text: Rule in loose case not brought to court

indicators.note: the letter for rule goes inside the word for loose

parts.note: untied means loose, not fastened

explanation.surface: A ruling in a messy legal case that never reached the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' tells you what the definition describes: a case not brought to court is an untried one.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that has not been heard by a judge has not yet been tried.

clue.text: Unreliable atlas bound to show antiquated name for African country

indicators.note: an unreliable map scrambles places, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An out-of-date atlas will show an old name for an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Basutoland was the colonial name of the southern African country now called Lesotho.

clue.text: Old sea dog

parts.note: an old sea wanderer or pirate, and also a common name for a pet dog

explanation.surface: A veteran sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea rover is an old word for a pirate, and Rover is the classic name for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover was a pirate roaming the seas, and the same word is a traditional dog's name.

clue.text: O'Connor Socrates — not so daft philosopher

parts.note: Des O'Connor was a British TV entertainer and singer

indicators.note: daft means crazy, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not tells us to take the word so out of the name Socrates

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Des O'Connor thought Socrates not so silly a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing SO from SOCRATES leaves CRATES, which 'daft' rearranges to CARTES.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes was a French philosopher, author of 'I think, therefore I am'.

clue.text: Following Arbuckle's lead, the metamorphosis of Chaplin, a true star

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the first letter of the name
the lead of the name is its first letter
a metamorphosis is a transformation, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: Fatty Arbuckle leads, then Chaplin transforms into a genuine film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Arbuckle and Chaplin were silent film stars, which makes 'star' look like a film star; it is a real star.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha Centauri is the nearest star system to the Sun, so it is a celestial star.

clue.text: Writer's profession lacking new hip art's development

indicators.note: the profession word goes without the letter for new

parts.note: a calling is a vocation or profession

indicators.note: development means turning into something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer's career loses its novelty when hip art develops.
explanation.walkthrough: CALLING less N gives CALLIG; 'development' rearranges HIPARTS to RAPHIST. 'Writer's' is the definition with 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A calligraphist is a person who writes in decorative handwriting, a kind of writer.

clue.text: Nipper caught barber dressed in short gown

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the shortened gown
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a robe is a long gown

indicators.note: dressed means prepared or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A child got caught by the barber while wearing a short gown.
explanation.walkthrough: A nipper looks like a child; here it is a crustacean that nips with its claws. 'dressed' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion into ROB.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber crab is a large land crab, and crabs nip with their claws.

clue.text: Tack that's more than near the knuckle!

definitions.text: Tack that's more than near the knuckle!

parts.words: Tack that's more than near the knuckle!
parts.note: tack means food, and near the knuckle means risqué; here the food literally includes a leg joint

explanation.surface: A joke that goes beyond risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near the knuckle' means indecent, but this Italian dish is braised veal shank cut through the bone, so it really is knuckle. Tack is food, as in hardtack.
explanation.definitionFit: Osso buco is an Italian dish of veal shanks containing the bone and marrow, food from right at the joint.

clue.text: Composer of 'Give Ireland Back To The Irish' and 'Eleanor Rigby'

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters running across the song titles

explanation.surface: A question about who wrote two songs, one by Wings and one by the Beatles.
explanation.walkthrough: Both songs are by Paul McCartney, which tempts you there; the composer is hidden across the titles.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the Baroque composer of Messiah.

clue.text: How opening of 'Star Trek' spelled out sequel

indicators.note: a spell transforms things, so these letters are put into a new order
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: How the opening words of Star Trek were spelled out in a follow-up.
explanation.walkthrough: HOW + S + TREK rearranged gives the title of the 2004 animated sequel.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrek 2 was the follow-up film to the animated hit Shrek, so it is a sequel.

clue.text: Sweet so good they named it twice

indicators.note: the phrase from the song about New York tells us to write the word two times

parts.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A sweet so good its name was said twice, like New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonbon is a small sugary confection, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Close bond that's fashioned with retirement in mind

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is a link or bond

explanation.surface: A close relationship that was formed with retiring from work in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment designed to be worn to bed when one retires for the night.

clue.text: Change of heart tends mostly to portend evil

indicators.note: a change of the word heart rearranges its letters
mostly means only the greater part of the word tends is kept

explanation.surface: A change of heart usually signals something bad is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of' rearranges HEART to THREA; 'mostly' keeps TEN, the bulk of TENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten is to be a sign of coming danger, to bode ill.

clue.text: Essential ingredient of philtre? A clear sticky goo

indicators.note: the answer sits at the heart of the words, an ingredient within them

explanation.surface: Asks what goes into a love potion: a clear sticky goo.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a thick syrup, a sticky substance made from sugar refining.

clue.text: Deploying grit then force is not Labour's inclination

indicators.note: deploying means arranging into position, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Using determination and then strength is not the Labour Party's way.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the UK's main centre-left party, so its inclination is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-leaning position in politics is the opposite of Labour's leftward tendency.

clue.text: What a buttoned-up 18 might be?

parts.note: a nightdress that is properly fastened, and also one made so it will not catch fire

explanation.surface: A question about how a prim nightdress might be described.
explanation.walkthrough: Buttoned-up means prim, keeping passion in check; nightwear is also treated so it does not burn. 18 is NIGHTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is treated to resist burning, and a prim garment holds back the fire of passion.

clue.text: Radio's top dog

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a peak is a top or summit

explanation.surface: A radio station's top dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peke is short for Pekingese, a small breed of dog.

clue.text: See 22
Relative's confused when a right is disregarded

indicators.note: the letters for a and right are ignored and taken out

parts.note: unclear means confused or muddled

explanation.surface: A relative is confused when their rights are ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative's' is the definition with 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a family member, the brother of a parent.

clue.text: Bad emotional experience foolishly starts quarrel

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A bad emotional experience foolishly begins an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is slang for a grudge or quarrel.

clue.text: Five crack police confronting regular peddler with old bike

indicators.note: confronting means facing, so the first pieces stand before the last

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: crack means break, so the letters are shattered and reassembled
regular letters are every other one, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Five elite police officers face a regular drug dealer with an old bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack police' looks like an elite squad; 'crack' rearranges POLICE to ELOCIP, and 'regular' picks EDE from peddler.
explanation.definitionFit: A velocipede is an early bicycle of the nineteenth century, an old bike.
